detailed_description:
The target video is a living sumi ink painting in <Subject 2>: every stroke keeps its wet brushed texture as it moves, ink flows and drips like real liquid ink on paper, and the hairline moon and cloud outlines stay thin, clean and steady.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. The black crow beats its wide wings in strong, heavy, unhurried strokes and rises toward the upper right, flying into the face of the moon. Its streaming ink trail thins into one long tapered brush stroke behind it, shedding a line of ink drops that fall slowly toward the bottom of the paper. As the crow crosses the moon, the white paper around the moon softly dims into a pale grey wash so the moon disc glows bright white, and the hairline clouds stretch out and drift slowly across both sides. The camera pulls back at slow speed in one continuous move, the moon and the crow growing smaller as wide empty paper opens around them. The camera is still pulling back as the shot ends on <Picture 2>, the crow silhouetted across the moon. No cut or transition occurs.

Deep rhythmic wingbeats push the air and slowly fade with distance. A distant caw echoes once, a soft night wind sighs, and ink drops patter faintly onto the paper below.
